catalog_citation: Saxena, Anju, Anna Sjöberg & Padam Sagar. 2022. The sound system of Kanashi. In Anju Saxena & Lars Borin (eds.), Synchronic and Diachronic Aspects of Kanashi (Trends in Linguistics. Documentation 38), 13-52. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton. ISBN 978-3-11-070…
catalog_locator: ch. 2 'The sound system of Kanashi' (Saxena, Sjöberg & Sagar), sec. 2.1 Transcriptions, p. 15; fn. 12, p. 29; closing areal discussion, pp. 49-50
catalog_quote: Unless otherwise stated, Kanashi examples are provided here in phonemic transcription, using the phoneme inventory presented in Sections 2.2 and 2.3. Stress is not indicated, as at this stage, we are not certain of its phonemic status. ... [fn. 12, p. 29:] As there is a possibility of vowels in unstressed positions behaving differently (e.g. vowel reduction), we have considered here only monosyllabic words. ... [pp. 49-50:] Many ST languages have phonemic tone and/or voice register distinctions. ... The Indosphere lies west of the Brahmaputra and is characterized by Hindu-Buddhist traditions and its languages are atonal (or incipiently tonal) and polysyllabic. ... Kanashi lies clearly in the so called Indosphere. Thus, from that point of view, it is not surprising that Kanashi is atonal and polysyllabic.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: all three loci confirmed verbatim in the OAPEN PDF we hold/text of Saxena, Sjöberg & Sagar 2022 (p. 15, fn. 12 p. 29, pp. 49-50). The deciding source is the modern fieldwork phonology chapter (2022), Glottolog's top-ranked and only 'phonology' item; the companion 2022 grammar sketch in the same held volume is also silent on stress. sources.quote: 'Tones and accent.—Tones are said to be a prominent feature of the dialect. It has not, however, been possible to lay down rules for their use. The accent is usually thrown as far back as possible.' (based on specimens supplied by G.C.L. Howell, who 'has not as yet been able to make a thorough study of Kanashi', p. 442). Read on the rendered page image, not just scanned.

sources.note: Only other grammar-length treatment (95 pp); Sharma's Part I sketches (held scanned) each carry an 'Accent' section (Pattani 2.8.3 'prominent accent on the initial syllable', Gahri 2.6), so Part II very likely states a Kanashi accent rule that our not determinable record lacks; would let us check the LSI 1909 'accent thrown as far back as possible' hint.
